clues: This is a capital city in the northwest of Argentina. It sits at the foot of a long mountain range.
Summers here often climb past 45 degrees, yet almost all the rain falls in those same hot months. Winters stay mild.
Juan Ramírez de Velasco, a Spanish soldier, founded this city in 1591. He named it for his home land in Spain.
People here still sing chaya music and love a festival called Tinkunaco. These songs and this feast sit at the heart of local life here.
This town loves sport and its fans cheer loud in one big ground. That ground has a long proud name, Estadio Carlos Augusto Mercado Luna.
